_howto: Settings tours. steps = page tour (first visit). sections = one tour per Settings area, starts the first time that area is opened (trigger = the area's page-section when active). guides = hands-on how-to guides in the ? menu (mode click = the user clicks the real button). To announce something NEW, add a step with a NEW id to the right tour. Rewording keeps the id. Never reuse an id.
title: Settings tour
whatsNewText: We've added something new here since you last took the tour.

steps.title: Welcome to Settings
steps.text:
This is where your company's system is set up: your company details, who can log in and what they can do, connections to other systems, clocking devices and more.

Use Next and Back, or your arrow keys. Press Esc to close.

steps.title: All Settings areas
steps.text: Every Settings area is listed here. You only see the areas your role allows.

steps.title: Company Profile
steps.text: Your company's name, contact details and logo.

steps.title: Connectivity
steps.text: Email sending, single sign-on with Microsoft or Google, the ZKTeco API, legacy and Sage links, and mobile app security.

steps.title: Sync Engine
steps.text: Mobile app preferences, which departments are synced, and a manual sync button.

steps.title: User Access
steps.text: Everyone who can log in: create users, link them to employees, and set which modules and data they can see.

steps.title: Roles & Permissions
steps.text: Ready-made permission sets. Give a user a role instead of ticking every permission by hand.

steps.title: Access Zones
steps.text: Group your clocking devices by place, such as Main Gate or Warehouse A.

steps.title: Hardware
steps.text: Clocking terminals, facial recognition licences, connected phones and CSV imports.

steps.title: Mobile Errors
steps.text: Error reports sent in by the mobile app, so problems on phones can be found and fixed.

steps.title: Usage & Quota
steps.text: How much of your licence you are using.

steps.title: Audit Trail
steps.text: A record of who changed what in the system, and when.

steps.title: Mobile Transactions
steps.text: The data phones have sent in (clockings, trips and more), so you can check what arrived.

steps.title: My Tickets
steps.text: Your support tickets with TNA Africa and their status.

steps.title: Notifications
steps.text: Automatic reminders and alerts, for example about clocking problems.

steps.title: Make more room
steps.text: Collapse the menu to icons only, and click again to open it. Your choice is remembered.

steps.title: Where you are
steps.text: The name of the area that is open right now.

steps.title: Your menu
steps.text: Click your name to open your menu. Let's look inside.

steps.title: Toggle Theme
steps.text: Switch between dark and light. Your choice follows your login to any computer.

steps.title: Launchpad
steps.text: Back to your home screen with all your modules.

steps.title: Help & Tours
steps.text: Opens the same Help & guides panel as the ? at the top right: tours, what's new and how-to guides.

steps.title: Logout
steps.text: Always log out on a shared computer.

steps.title: Search any screen
steps.text:
Type what you're looking for, like leave or roster, to jump straight to any screen you have access to, in any module.

Point at the search bar without typing to see your most visited screens, and pin your favourites.

steps.title: Your menu
steps.text: Click your name for your profile, other areas of the system, and logout. Let's look inside.

steps.title: Launchpad
steps.text: Back to your home screen with all your modules.

steps.title: Profile
steps.text: Your account: your name, role and when you last signed in. Update your name and email, see your employee record, or change your password on the Security tab. Saving any change asks for your current password, so nobody else can change your account.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Company-wide setup. Only shown to users allowed to change settings.

steps.title: ESS
steps.text: Your own self service: leave, claims, payslips and documents.

steps.title: Connect a Phone
steps.text: Shows a QR code that connects a company phone to your company. It contains your licence key, so only show it while setting up phones.

steps.title: Download the App
steps.text: Shows a QR code to download the Android app onto a phone.

steps.title: Help & Tours
steps.text: Opens the same Help & guides panel as the ? at the top right.

steps.title: Dark Mode
steps.text: Switch between dark and light. Your choice follows your login to any computer.

steps.title: Logout
steps.text: Always log out on a shared computer.

steps.title: Help is always here
steps.text: Click ? (top right, next to your profile) to open Help & guides: search for what you want to do, tour the area you're in or any other Settings area, see what's new, and read the how-to guides step by step.

steps.title: You're all set
steps.text: Each Settings area also has its own short tour. It starts the first time you open that area, and you can replay it any time from ? at the top right, under Tour an area.

steps.title: Company Entities
steps.text: Your active company, with its contact details and logo.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Find a company by name.

steps.title: Create Company
steps.text: Add a new company entity.

steps.title: Your company
steps.text: The name, contact email, contact number and logo. Use Edit on the row to change them, including uploading a new logo. The new logo is used across the system.

steps.title: Deactivated Entities
steps.text: Companies that have been switched off. They are kept here for your records.

steps.title: Five tabs
steps.text: Connectivity is split into tabs: Email Config, SSO Identity, ZKTeco API, Legacy Systems and Mobile Security. Let's go through each one.

steps.title: Email Config
steps.text: Your own mail server for system emails like password resets and notifications. Leave it blank to use TNA Africa's standard email. Click Edit to change it, then Save.

steps.title: Send Test Email
steps.text: Send a test message to check your email settings work before you rely on them.

steps.title: SSO Identity
steps.text: Let staff sign in with their Microsoft or Google work account instead of a separate password. Enter the Application (Client) ID from Microsoft or Google here.

steps.title: ZKTeco API
steps.text: The connection to your ZKTeco server: its address (Base URL) and access token. After saving, use Test API Connection to check it answers.

steps.title: CVS Access Zones
steps.text: Pulls the access levels from ZKTeco so you can give them to employees in Employee Master.

steps.title: Direct CVS Database Link
steps.text: An optional direct link to the CVS database. Edit the details, save, then use Test Connection.

steps.title: Sage Integration
steps.text: Connects to Sage payroll. Set the login details, which system is the master, and what is pushed to Sage (leave, payroll costs) or pulled from it (wage advice, pay rates, leave balances). Use Test Connection after saving.

steps.title: Sage Leave Type Mapping
steps.text: Click Load from Sage, then match each of your leave types to the Sage one. Suggested matches are filled in but only saved when you click Save Mapping.

steps.title: Mobile Security
steps.text: Choose how phones may connect: HTTPS only (secure, recommended), HTTP only, or both.

steps.title: Three tabs
steps.text: Mobile App Prefs, Hierarchy Constraints and Manual Sync.

steps.title: Hide Restricted Tiles
steps.text: When this is on, tiles an employee can't use are hidden in the mobile app instead of greyed out. It saves as soon as you switch it.

steps.title: Root Department
steps.text: Limit syncing to one ZKTeco department code and everything under it (for example 1000). Leave it blank to sync the whole organisation.

steps.title: Sync method
steps.text: Choose where employee data comes from: Use API pulls it from your ZKTeco server, Use Own DB keeps this system as the master.

steps.title: Force Master Sync
steps.text: Pull employees now instead of waiting for the automatic sync. Handy after adding people in ZKTeco.

steps.title: Create User
steps.text: Opens the form for a new login. For a step-by-step walkthrough, open ? and choose User Access & creating a user under How-to guides.

steps.title: Data Tools
steps.text: Export Report is in here now: every user with their role and password status - handy for access audits. Export This View downloads only the users the list shows, with your columns in your order. Download Blank Template gives you an Excel file with the import columns and your role list. Fill it in, then use Bulk Import Users to upload it (.xlsx or .csv) and create many users at once.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Find a user by name, username or email as you type.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Filter by User Type (system logins or users linked to an employee) and by Assigned Role. The number shows how many filters are on.

steps.title: Columns
steps.text: Choose which columns to show and drag them into your order. There are extra columns too, like Username, Linked Employee ID and Mobile Tiles. Your layout is remembered for you on any computer.

steps.title: The user list
steps.text: Each user's status, how they may log in (web, mobile), their role, which departments' data they can see, and their modules. Click a heading to sort, drag a heading to move it, type in the box under a heading to search that column, or right-click a heading to choose columns.

steps.title: Edit a user
steps.text: Opens the user in three tabs: Profile & Security, Data Scopes (which departments' data they can see) and Module Restrictions.

steps.title: Deactivate or activate
steps.text: Deactivating stops the user logging in. You can activate them again at any time.

steps.title: Change many users at once
steps.text: Tick users (or this box for all of them) and a toolbar appears to Apply Role, Update Modules or reset them to the Default Password. It applies to everyone ticked, so check the count first.

steps.title: Create Role
steps.text: Give the role a code and a name, choose whether it allows Web and/or Mobile access, then tick its permissions on each tab: Time & Attendance, Employee Master, Employee Costs, HR, System Config, Settings, ESS Master, Access Control, Reports and App Modules.

steps.title: Your roles
steps.text: Every role in your company. Give a role to a user in User Access, either on the user or for many users at once with Apply Role.

steps.title: Edit a role
steps.text: Change the role's name, access and permissions. Everyone with this role is affected, so check before you remove anything.

steps.title: Step-by-step guides
steps.text: Open ? > How-to guides for hands-on walkthroughs: Create a role, Give a user a role and Give many users a role at once. Search for role to find them.

steps.title: Create a zone
steps.text:
A zone groups clocking devices by place, for example Main Gate or Warehouse A. Type a name and click Create Zone.

Employees are then linked to zones in Employee Master, which decides the devices they can use.

steps.title: Your zones
steps.text: Each zone and the devices connected to it. Use edit to change its devices, or the bin to delete the zone.

steps.title: Four tabs
steps.text: Hardware Terminals, Facial AI Licenses, Connected Mobile Devices and CSV Imports.

steps.title: Your clocking devices
steps.text: The devices TNA Africa has assigned to your company, with their serial number, IP address and whether they are online. Rename a device and put it in your Access Zones here.

steps.title: Device actions
steps.text: Remote actions for that device, such as unlock, reboot, enrol a face, sync the time, recover logs and sync employee biometrics. The options depend on the device type. Clear Admins and Wipe Logs can't be undone.

steps.title: Facial AI Licenses
steps.text: Codes that switch on face recognition on a phone or tablet, even offline. Each code can be used once and then belongs to that device. The count shows how many you have used.

steps.title: Connected Mobile Devices
steps.text: Every phone and tablet that has connected to your company, with the last user and when it was last seen. Useful when a phone isn't syncing.

steps.title: CSV Imports
steps.text: When a phone can't sync, use Export Unsynced Data on the phone and load that file here. Clock punches and fuel transactions are imported as if the phone had synced. You see a preview first, and can download any rows that need attention.

steps.title: Problems reported from phones
steps.text: When something goes wrong in the mobile app, the user can report it and it lands here: who reported it, what happened, the phone model, when, and whether it's been dealt with.

steps.title: View a report
steps.text: Opens the full report so you can see exactly what the user saw.

steps.title: Mark as resolved
steps.text: Once the problem is sorted, mark it resolved so the list only shows what still needs attention.

steps.title: Refresh
steps.text: Load the latest reports.

steps.title: How usage is counted
steps.text:
Your usage is counted on active employees and active assets. To keep it accurate, terminate employees who have left in Employee Master, and mark assets you no longer use as inactive.

For billing questions, contact your TNA Africa partner.

steps.title: Filter the log
steps.text: Choose a date range and, if you like, one user, then click Filter.

steps.title: Every change, recorded
steps.text: Each change made in the system: when, by whom, what they did, in which module, and the details of what changed.

steps.title: More results
steps.text: The log is shown a page at a time. Use Prev and Next to move through it.

steps.title: Export PDF
steps.text: Save the filtered log as a PDF, for example for an auditor.

steps.title: Find a sync
steps.text: Each time a phone syncs it sends a batch of records. Narrow the list by date range, user or device, then click Filter.

steps.title: Only the problems
steps.text: Choose Contains Errors to see only batches where some records failed. This is the quickest way to trace a missing clocking.

steps.title: Sync batches
steps.text: When each batch arrived, who sent it from which device, and how many records succeeded or failed.

steps.title: Look inside a batch
steps.text: See every record in the batch and why any of them failed.

steps.title: Your open support tickets
steps.text: A read-only list of your active support requests with TNA Africa: the ticket number, when it was opened, the module, the problem, who is working on it and its status.

steps.title: Refresh
steps.text: Load the latest status of your tickets.

steps.title: Scheduled notifications
steps.text: This is where company notifications are set up: your own message to the phone and / or by email, on the days and times you choose, to departments, shifts or chosen employees.

steps.title: New schedule
steps.text: Click New schedule to write a message and pick who gets it and when. Add a condition such as only if not clocked in yet to send clock-in reminders.

steps.title: A tidier schedule editor
steps.text: New and Edit now open in tabs - Schedule, Who gets it, Conditions and Message - with switches instead of tick boxes. The line at the bottom sums up what will be sent before you press Save. See the how-to guide Set up a scheduled notification under ? at the top right.

steps.title: Is the phone push working?
steps.text: This small circle shows it at a glance: green = push ready, amber = not set up yet (phones use their own alarm), red = push stopped and needs attention. Click it for the details and how the timing works.

steps.title: Your schedules
steps.text: Every schedule is listed here. Edit, pause or delete one at any time.

guides.title: Edit your company details
guides.blurb: Open your company and change its name, contact details or logo.

steps.title: Company Profile
steps.text: Everything about your company lives here. Click this menu item to open the screen.

steps.title: Edit your company
steps.text: This opens the editor where you can change the company name, contact details and logo. Click Edit to finish.

guides.title: User Access & creating a user
guides.blurb: Every control on User Access, then set up a new user step by step.

steps.title: User Access
steps.text: This is where every person who can log into the system is managed. Click it to open the screen.

steps.title: Search
steps.text: Filters the list as you type, matching against name, username or email address. Useful once you have more than a screenful of users.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Opens a panel with two filters. User Type separates system-only logins from users linked to an employee record. Assigned Role narrows to one role, or to users on custom permissions with no role at all. The badge shows how many filters are active.

steps.title: Columns
steps.text: Pick the columns you want and drag them into your order, including extras like Username and Linked Employee ID. It is remembered for you.

steps.title: The user table
steps.text: Access shows which channels the user can log into, Data Scope which departments their data is limited to, and Modules which parts of the system they see. Click a heading to sort, drag it to move it, and use the box under a heading to search just that column.

steps.title: Bulk selection
steps.text: Ticking this selects every user in the list, and each row has its own checkbox too. As soon as one is selected, a toolbar appears above the table. Let's look at it.

steps.title: The bulk toolbar
steps.text:
Shown here for the guide. Normally it only appears once users are selected, and the count on the left tells you how many.

Apply Role gives the chosen role to everyone selected, or removes it if you pick Remove Role. Update Modules sets which modules they can see without touching their roles. Default Password resets them all to the system default, which stops their current passwords working straight away.

Everything here applies to every selected user at once, so check that count first.

steps.title: Exporting
steps.text: Both exports are under Data Tools. Export Report gives every user with their role and password status - handy for access audits. Export This View gives only the users the list shows (search, filters and sort), with your columns in your order.

steps.title: Create User
steps.text: Now the main part. Click here to open the new user form.

steps.title: Username
steps.text: What the person types at the login screen. It must be unique in your company and shouldn't be changed later, so agree a naming convention before you start.

steps.title: Email address
steps.text: Used for password resets and system notifications. Use a real address the person checks. With a wrong email here they can't recover their own account.

steps.title: First and last name
steps.text: The name shown in the menu, on audit records and anywhere their actions are logged. This is what other people see, not the username.

steps.title: Temporary password
steps.text: The password you give them for their first login. Share it securely and have them change it once they are in.

steps.title: Base Role
steps.text: The most important field. A role carries a ready-made permission set, so picking one saves ticking dozens of boxes. It also pre-selects the modules on the next tab. Leave it blank only if this user really needs a one-off custom set.

steps.title: Linked Employee Profile
steps.text: Links this login to an employee by name or PIN. Once linked, the user can see their own timesheet, leave and payslips in ESS. Leave it empty for admin-only logins that aren't on the payroll.

steps.title: Access channels
steps.text: Web Dashboard allows browser login. Mobile App allows the phone app. Force Direct ESS Login sends them straight into self service. Use it for staff who should only ever see their own information.

steps.title: Web Modules tab
steps.text: Access channels decide whether they can log in. Modules decide what they see once they do. Click this tab.

steps.title: Web modules
steps.text: Each tick adds a tile to their Launchpad. If you chose a Base Role these already match it, so only change them when one person needs something extra or something removed.

steps.title: Mobile & ESS tab
steps.text: The last tab covers everything on the phone. Click it.

steps.title: ESS features
steps.text: What this person may do on their own record: clock in and out, log trips, request leave, submit claims. These only ever apply to themselves.

steps.title: Mobile tiles
steps.text: The buttons on the app home screen. These are work tools rather than personal: clocking other staff, capturing piece work, logging fuel, recording violations. Supervisors need them, ordinary ESS users don't.

steps.title: Create Profile
steps.text: This saves the user, and they can log in straight away with the temporary password. Nothing has been created by this guide, so close the form if you were only looking.

guides.title: Set up a scheduled notification
guides.blurb: Send a clock-in or any other reminder to the phone and / or by email on the days and time you choose.

steps.title: Notifications
steps.text: Scheduled notifications live here. Click this menu item to open the screen.

steps.title: New schedule
steps.text: This opens the schedule editor. To change one you already have, use the Edit button on its row instead.

steps.title: Schedule
steps.text: Give it a name, tap the days it should go out (or use Weekdays / Every day), and set the time. From and Until are optional - leave them empty to keep it running. Switched on lets you pause it later without removing it.

steps.title: Who gets it
steps.text: Next, choose who receives it.

steps.title: Departments, shifts or employees
steps.text: Switch between Departments, Shifts and Employees and flick on the ones you want. Anyone who matches any of them gets it. The numbers show how many you picked in each.

steps.title: Conditions
steps.text: Conditions decide who is skipped on the day.

steps.title: Only send if / leave out
steps.text: For a clock-in reminder switch on They have not clocked in yet today. Leaving out people on leave and days off stops reminders going to people who aren't working.

steps.title: Message
steps.text: Last, write what they will see.

steps.title: Phone and email
steps.text: Switch on Phone notification, Email or both, and write each message. The tags under Personalise (like {first_name} or {shift_start}) are filled in for every person.

steps.title: Check the summary
steps.text: This line sums up the whole schedule - days, time, who and how. Anything missing shows in orange.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Saves the schedule. Nothing has been saved by this guide, so press Cancel if you were only looking. After saving, use the Send test to me button on its row to try it on your own phone and email.

guides.title: Create a role (permissions)
guides.blurb: Make a role with the screens and rights a group of people needs, e.g. Line Manager or Payroll Clerk.

steps.title: Roles & Permissions
steps.text: Roles live here. A role is a set of permissions you give to many users at once. Click this menu item to open the screen.

steps.title: Your roles
steps.text: Every role in your company. Editing a role later (the Edit button on its row) changes it for every user who has that role straight away, so check who uses it before you take anything away.

steps.title: Create Role
steps.text: Opens the role form.

steps.title: Code and name
steps.text: Role Code is a short unique code, e.g. LINE_MGR. Role Name is what people see in lists, e.g. Line Manager.

steps.title: Web and Mobile access
steps.text: Whether people with this role may log in on the web dashboard, the mobile app, or both.

steps.title: Permission tabs
steps.text: One tab per part of the system: Time & Attendance, Employee Master, Employee Costs, HR, System Config, Settings, ESS Master, Access Control, Reports and App Modules. Go through each one the role needs.

steps.title: Open a tab
steps.text: Let's look at one.

steps.title: Everything on this tab
steps.text: Ticks every permission on this tab in one go. Handy for a full-access role; otherwise tick only what is needed below.

steps.title: Screens and rights
steps.text: Each Tab: line is a screen the person can open. The lines under it (└─) are extra rights on that screen, such as editing, exporting or importing. Leave those off for a view-only role.

steps.title: Save Role
steps.text:
Saves the role. Nothing has been saved by this guide, so press Cancel if you were only looking.

Next: give the role to people - see the guides Give a user a role and Give many users a role at once.

guides.title: Give a user a role
guides.blurb: Set one person's role, then choose whose data they may see with Data Scopes.

steps.title: User Access
steps.text: Roles are given to people on User Access. Click this menu item to open the screen.

steps.title: Edit a user
steps.text: Open the person you want to change. Use the search above the list to find them first if needed.

steps.title: System Role
steps.text: Pick the role here. Picking a role also sets this person's module ticks to match it, and removes any Custom Overrides they had. -- Custom / No Role -- means no role.

steps.title: Data Scopes
steps.text: A role says what someone can do. Data Scopes say whose data they can see.

steps.title: Whose data they see
steps.text: Tick the departments (and, if you use them, geographic areas) this person may see. When the Data Visibility Mode box shows, you can instead limit them to their direct reportees or their full downline.

steps.title: Module Restrictions
steps.text: Last, check the modules.

steps.title: Modules
steps.text: These were filled in from the role you picked: the web modules, ESS features and mobile app tiles. Change them only if this one person needs something different.

steps.title: Save User Profile
steps.text: Saves the user. Nothing has been saved by this guide, so press Cancel if you were only looking. To give a role to many people at once, see Give many users a role at once.

guides.title: Give many users a role at once
guides.blurb: Tick users and apply (or remove) a role for all of them in one go.

steps.title: User Access
steps.text: Bulk changes are made on User Access. Click this menu item to open the screen.

steps.title: Narrow the list
steps.text: Tip: search, use Filters or the search under a column heading first, so the list shows only the people you want to change.

steps.title: Tick the users
steps.text: Tick each person to change, or the box in the heading row to tick everyone in the list.

steps.title: The bulk toolbar
steps.text: It appears as soon as someone is ticked. The number on the left is how many users the change will apply to - check it.

steps.title: Choose the role
steps.text: Pick the role to give everyone ticked. Choose -- Remove Role -- to take their role away instead.

steps.title: Apply Role
steps.text: Asks you to confirm, then applies the role (or removes it) for every ticked user. This guide does not press it - nothing has been changed.

steps.title: Untick when done
steps.text: Untick the users when you are finished, so the next bulk change doesn't go to the same people by accident. For one person's Data Scopes (whose data they see), use Edit on that user - see Give a user a role.
